verses.text: When all this was over, all the Israelites who were there went out to the towns of Judah. They smashed the stone pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the hilltop shrines and altars all through Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the Israelites went back to their own towns and their own land.

Hezekiah organized the priests and Levites into their groups, each with their own work. Some offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Others served, gave thanks, and sang praises at the gates of the LORD's temple.

The king gave animals from his own property for the burnt offerings: for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and for the burnt offerings on the Sabbaths, at the New Moon festivals, and at the other set festivals, as written in the LORD's law.
He also ordered the people living in Jerusalem to give the priests and Levites their share, so they could give all their time to the LORD's law.

As soon as the order went out, the Israelites gave generously from the first part of their harvest: grain, new wine, olive oil, honey, and everything the fields produced. They brought a large amount, a tenth of everything.

The people of Israel and Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tenth of their cattle and sheep, and a tenth of the holy things set apart for the LORD their God. They piled them up in heaps.
They began making the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh month.
When Hezekiah and the leaders came and saw the heaps, they praised the LORD and blessed his people Israel.
Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps.

Azariah the chief priest, from Zadok's family, answered, "Since the people began bringing their gifts to the LORD's temple, we have had enough to eat and plenty left over, because the LORD has blessed his people. This huge amount is what is left."
Then Hezekiah ordered them to prepare storerooms in the LORD's temple, and they did.
They faithfully brought in the gifts, the tenths, and the holy things. Conaniah the Levite was in charge of them, and his brother Shimei was second in charge.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were supervisors under Conaniah and his brother Shimei. King Hezekiah and Azariah, the official in charge of God's temple, appointed them.
Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the East Gate, was in charge of the gifts people chose to give to God. He handed out the gifts given to the LORD and the most holy things.
Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah. They worked faithfully in the towns of the priests, giving shares to their relatives by their groups, to old and young alike.
They also gave shares to the males three years old and older who were listed in the family records, everyone who went into the LORD's temple to do their daily work, by their groups and duties.
They gave shares to the priests listed by their families, and to the Levites twenty years old and older, by their duties and groups.
They also gave to the little children, wives, sons, and daughters listed in the family records of the whole community, because they had faithfully kept themselves holy.

For the priests, the descendants of Aaron, who lived in the farm lands around their towns, men were chosen by name in every town to give shares to every male among the priests and to everyone listed in the records of the Levites.
Hezekiah did this all through Judah. He did what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.
Everything he started to do for the service of God's temple, and in obeying the law and commands, he did with all his heart to seek his God. And he was successful.
